name: Class Declaration
definition: Holds each declared class of action, with whether it needs the authorization of the user and with the writer that declared it. Accepts the declaration of a class, a change to a class and the removal of a class. Gives the declared classes to a caller.
rationale: DEC-116 makes this system the one holder of the class, and DEC-032 gives the reason: a class that each boundary keeps for itself becomes one policy for each boundary. REQ-PL-013 names three classes that the user states as a hard boundary, and a class that nobody declared cannot be compared against an action. FUN-WC-08 holds the declared resources and FUN-ST-10 holds the declared kinds in the same shape, so a declaration held here adds no body under DEC-024. DEC-055 removes a class by the path that declared it, so the removal is a capability of this function and not a second one. REQ-AU-006 gives the classes to a caller, and DEC-069 keeps them out of the rules of REQ-PL-027, and MET-017 uses the functions as the coverage check, so a capability that no function states is invisible to that check. FUN-AD-04 states the same clause for a position. REQ-ST-031 holds the writer with each declared kind and this function does the same for a class. The first text held only a class that needs the authorization of the user. DEC-109 adds a class that states that an act needs none.

name: Classification
definition: Gives, for an act that a caller called and the arguments of that act, whether the act is in a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 makes the platform tell the difference between an action that needs the authorization of the user and an action that does not. DEC-019 declares in one place and refuses in many, so the caller states the action and this system answers. The object is stated with the action because a class of REQ-PL-013 cannot be judged from the action alone: to send a message to the user and to send a message to a third party are one action with two objects. DEC-057 makes the act exist before the request, so the caller states an action that it prepared. The first text said an action and its object. DEC-103 judges the act with its arguments.

name: Admission by Position
definition: Refuses an act that it holds from a caller whose position does not admit the act, and a released gated unit whose raiser holds a position that does not admit its act.
rationale: DEC-019 declares the position in one place and makes each boundary refuse, and DEC-029 makes the declaration of a class an act. FUN-ST-07, FUN-WC-05 and FUN-AD-06 are the same function at the other declaration boundaries, and this system held none. DEC-116 keeps the class in one place and does not state who may write it, so without this function any caller that reaches this system declares a class and stops the actions of another agent. The first text named only the acts on a class. DEC-114 adds the parties and DEC-111 makes this system accept a call only from Actuation.

name: Copy and Restoration
definition: Gives a copy of the declared classes that is of a state that the system held at one time, and restores the declared classes from such a copy.
rationale: REQ-PL-022 names the declared classes, and DEC-116 makes this system their one holder, so no other compartment can state what a consistent copy of them is. FUN-AD-11 states the same capability for what states an agent and FUN-ST-08 for life state. OPN-040 asks whether the copy away from the host is one capability in External Access or one in each holder, and this function follows whatever that answer is.

name: User Parties
definition: Holds the parties that count as the user. Accepts their declaration, a change to them and their removal.
rationale: DEC-114. A class of REQ-PL-013 gates a message to a third party and not a message to the user, so a classification needs to know who the user is.
